text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
WeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
WellAttended(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
HasWedding(x) ::: x has a wedding.
Question:
Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? John has a larger family.
Predicates:
LargerFamily(john)
Premises:
∀x (WeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are people who are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → WeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others to come to their ceremony make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttended(x) → Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone who has a well-attended wedding invites others to come to their ceremony.
∃x (LargerFamily(x) ∧ WellAttended(x)) ::: Some people that have well-attended weddings have larger families.
If engaged(john) then ¬Invite(john, y) ∧ WeddingPlans(john) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends to their ceremony and make wedding plans.
If largerFamily(john) then (WellAttended(john) ∨ Invite(john, y)) ::: If John has a larger family, then either John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends to their ceremony.
Conclusion:
LargerFamily(john)
